**Genesis 1**

*In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.*

*2 And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.*

*3 And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.*

*4 And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness.*

*5 And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And the evening and the morning were the first day.*

*6 And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.*

*7 And God made the firmament, and divided the waters which were under the firmament from the waters which were above the firmament: and it was so.*

*8 And God called the firmament Heaven. And the evening and the morning were the second day.*

*9 And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so.*

*10 And God called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters called he Seas: and God saw that it was good.*

*11 And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed is in itself, upon the earth: and it was so.*

*12 And the earth brought forth grass, and herb yielding seed after his kind, and the tree yielding fruit, whose seed was in itself, after his kind: and God saw that it was good.*

*13 And the evening and the morning were the third day.*

*14 And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:*

*15 And let them be for lights in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth: and it was so.*

*16 And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.*

*17 And God set them in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth,*

*18 And to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness: and God saw that it was good.*

*19 And the evening and the morning were the fourth day.*

*20 And God said, Let the waters bring forth abundantly the moving creature that hath life, and fowl that may fly above the earth in the open firmament of heaven.*

*21 And God created great whales, and every living creature that moveth, which the waters brought forth abundantly, after their kind, and every winged fowl after his kind: and God saw that it was good.*

*22 And God blessed them, saying, Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let fowl multiply in the earth.*

*23 And the evening and the morning were the fifth day.*

*24 And God said, Let the earth bring forth the living creature after his kind, cattle, and creeping thing, and beast of the earth after his kind: and it was so.*

*25 And God made the beast of the earth after his kind, and cattle after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the earth after his kind: and God saw that it was good.*

*26 And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.*

*27 So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.*

*28 And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.*

*29 And God said, Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat.*

*30 And to every beast of the earth, and to every fowl of the air, and to every thing that creepeth upon the earth, wherein there is life, I have given every green herb for meat: and it was so.*
*31 And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. And the evening and the morning were the sixth day.*

This is creation. And Jesus was there. "Let Us make them in Our image," as man was spoken into creation on the 6th day and given dominion over all He created.

**John 1**
*In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made. In him was life; and the life was the light of men. And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.*

*And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.*

**Colossians 1**
*For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him: And he is before all things, and by him all things consist.*

*And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence. For it pleased the Father that in him should all fulness dwell; And, having made peace through the blood of his cross, by him to reconcile all things unto himself; by him, I say, whether they be things in earth, or things in heaven.*

**Ephesians 1**
*According as He hath chosen us in Him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love: Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will, To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved.*

**Revelation 1**
*I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty.*

**Hebrews 13**
*Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.*

Amen

Now, note the order of things. This is how all of creation was made. And the creation of days, separated from night, morning and evening, was created by God who is outside of time.

The fullness of the Godhead exists when nothing else did, including time, and through Him was created light, substance, life, and mankind. Everything after its own kind, with the seed contained therein propagating that life over time.

This is a literal story of creation, as it occurred roughly 6,200 years ago.

Not because of fossils found in weird places, or the problems with carbon dating, or the position of the stars in the firmament unchanging, or the complexity and variance of life.

But because God said this is how it happened. In His inspired and preserved word, The God who cannot lie tells us these things and that they are so.

Evolution, which is the worship of time, or Kronos as the creator, is literally the worship of the created, as we see in Genesis, because God created time. And so we know it's false.

Biblical inerrancy, and the fundamentalist belief that it is the inspired and preserved word of God, has yet to fail, even as science falsely so-called makes claims to the contrary, God's hand is revealed continually making the wise into fools.

This is why God's word is continually under attack. This is why doubt is continually sown. Because, if many have doubts about any aspect of God's word, then many will not believe the report. The Gospel, and will perish as sinners.

And while you don't have to necessarily believe in the literal biblical creation in order to believe that Jesus is the son of God who died for our sins and was resurrected again, and whom through which we are given Grace by God unto eternal life, it is difficult to then express that Faith to others while doubting much of His word. Or thinking it allegory, or some sort of parable.

The gospels give account back to Adam. The genealogies are there to mark time. And the generations from Noah back to Adam, from Abraham back to Noah, from Israel to Christ... These are there for a purpose.

And while there are some seeking to take away from God's word by casting doubt not just on the creation story but on every biblical text that draws upon it, all scripture that refers to it in describing Jesus Christ to us, there are people that seek to add to his word as well. It is easy to read into it things that are not there, and this too is an error.

So as we go forth through Genesis understand that it is not only the faith of this author, but my firm opinion that the Bible is literally true, and the truths revealed from Genesis 1 through the end in Revelation 22, is the story of Jesus Christ. God revealing His Son to us that we may believe and have eternal life.

It is God's word, His testimony, the testaments that He has given us to His promise for us. And from start to finish, Alpha to Omega it is one gospel, the good news of salvation through Christ Jesus.

**Genesis 2**

*Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them.*

*2 And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.*

*3 And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made.*

*4 These are the generations of the heavens and of the earth when they were created, in the day that the Lord God made the earth and the heavens,*

*5 And every plant of the field before it was in the earth, and every herb of the field before it grew: for the Lord God had not caused it to rain upon the earth, and there was not a man to till the ground.*

*6 But there went up a mist from the earth, and watered the whole face of the ground.*

*7 And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.*

*8 And the Lord God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.*

*9 And out of the ground made the Lord God to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.*

*10 And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads.*

*11 The name of the first is Pison: that is it which compasseth the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold;*

*12 And the gold of that land is good: there is bdellium and the onyx stone.*

*13 And the name of the second river is Gihon: the same is it that compasseth the whole land of Ethiopia.*

*14 And the name of the third river is Hiddekel: that is it which goeth toward the east of Assyria. And the fourth river is Euphrates.*

*15 And the Lord God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.*

*16 And the Lord God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat:*

*17 But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.*

*18 And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.*

*19 And out of the ground the Lord God formed every beast of the field, and every fowl of the air; and brought them unto Adam to see what he would call them: and whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof.*

*20 And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him.*

*21 And the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof;*

*22 And the rib, which the Lord God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.*

*23 And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.*

*24 Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.*

*25 And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed.*

Amen.

The stage is set. God and man and woman. The garden. The one law, told directly from God to Adam. Before Eve was made from him. Free from sin, naked and unashamed.

There are 66 chapters in Isaiah just like there are 66 books in the Bible. There are 39 books in OT, 27 in the NT. 39 of Isaiah's chapters deal with the concurrent events of those days (and glimpses of far future in end days), while 40 to 66 deal with the Messiah and his first and second coming. Some have gone far enough to say each chapter may correspond to their respective books in the Bible thematically, so in a way the books of Isaiah also prophetically matches the books of the Bible before it was completed.

**Genesis 3**

*Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?*

*2 And the woman said unto the serpent, We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden:*

*3 But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.*

*4 And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die:*

*5 For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.*

*6 And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.*

*7 And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons.*

*8 And they heard the voice of the Lord God walking in the garden in the cool of the day: and Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the Lord God amongst the trees of the garden.*

*9 And the Lord God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?*

*10 And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself.*

*11 And he said, Who told thee that thou wast naked? Hast thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldest not eat?*

*12 And the man said, The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.*

*13 And the Lord God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.*

*14 And the Lord God said unto the serpent, Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life:*

*15 And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.*

*16 Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.*

*17 And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life;*

*18 Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field;*

*19 In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.*

*20 And Adam called his wife's name Eve; because she was the mother of all living.*

*21 Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them.*

*22 And the Lord God said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil: and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever:*

*23 Therefore the Lord God sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken.*

*24 So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.*

**Romans 5:12-17**
*Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned: (for until the law sin was in the world: but sin is not imputed when there is no law. Nevertheless death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam's transgression, who is the figure of him that was to come. But not as the offence, so also is the free gift. For if through the offence of one many be dead, much more the grace of God, and the gift by grace, which is by one man, Jesus Christ, hath abounded unto many. And not as it was by one that sinned, so is the gift: for the judgment was by one to condemnation, but the free gift is of many offences unto justification. For if by one man's offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.*

And so, sin entered the world by the disobedience of one man, who knowingly violated the one command of God.

Adam, given the perfect situation, abundance of food, dominion, a perfect help meet for a wife, climate so perfect they could be naked, and the purity and innocence to not be ashamed of it. He knew God, could talk with Him and know he was loved by His creator more than anything else in creation. Paradise on earth with none of the cares of this world that we use as excuse and snares to trap us.

And had this been given without choice, without free will, the ability to choose, it would have been a prison. A cosmic dollhouse.

But God, as He made us in His image, made us with the capacity for will. Conscious of our own independent thought. Not simply a biped humanoid with a beard, the shell of the flesh, but like unto Him in that we can think, reason and have an independent soul. And thus, our own will. That is what makes us like unto God, made in his image. God the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit all have will to choose, the Bible tells us, and the Son and the Spirit do the will of the Father, by choice, as Jesus wept in prayer in the garden of Gethsemane, commiting Himself to the Father's will, not Jesus' own.

And so, Adam was given a choice. A law. A commandment to obey, with consequence if he chose not to.

In a garden, man made a choice to sin and disobey the will of God the Father, and in a garden, the Man, Christ Jesus chose to obey unto death.

*For if by one man's offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.*

Sin couldn't enter the world without choice. Sin couldn't be taken from the world without choice. A free gift cannot be received by force, or it is no longer free. It must be accepted by choice.

And so, God's first interaction with man was to provide him a choice. In the first few chapters of the first book of God's word, given to us by Him to know Him. And the choice of fallen man to believe that sure testimony, or not. To be like Eve, who was told of the command by Adam, and instead of believing God's word, was deceived.

And so, knowing that we have free will, knowing for certain that God has given us choice, and that ability to believe or disobey is ours, not His, we reject the damnable heresy of Calvinism, for it would deny Adam his choice to sin and make the suffering and sacrifice of Christ for that sin into some kind of sick joke.

Now, what was the command of God? **Genesis 2**:16-17;

*And the Lord God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat: But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.*

And we note this was given Adam, before Eve was. And told to Eve by Adam. Which is how God's word is given each of us. Spoken of the LORD God, by faith passed down to others, by faith received and believed. And it is that faith in the received word of God that Satan, more subtle than any beast, preys on, when as the serpent he comes to tempt Eve;

*And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?*

"Ye, hath God said?" This is Satan's oldest trick. Casting doubt upon God's word to get us to sin. This is the reason for false Bible versions. This is the way of false prophets. Making us doubt that God's word is pure and right.

"Many of the earliest manuscripts leave this passage out...this verse is not found in earlier manuscripts...the Greek here could actually mean this instead. Do you even know Hebrew?" Footnotes. Margin notes. "Study Bibles." "You need a seminary graduate with a doctorate in Divinity to understand the Bible!" "God of the OT is angry, but Jesus is love!" "That was written to people of *that* time, not to us!"

Fill in your own example of "Yea, hath God said..?" here.

*And the woman said unto the serpent, We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden: But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.*

*And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die: For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.*

The serpent misquotes and questions, Eve knows the truth of the word and corrects him. Then Satan incredulously casts more doubt.

And this doubt, we see work in Eve, sparking the curiosity and wonder and reason, gifts of God that make us like unto Him, but now, under our will and doubts sown by Satan, used to choose sin.

And so she *saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise*, and so curious and doubting, covetous of the wisdom of God, Eve was beguiled into sin, and ate of the tree.

And Adam? Eve *gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.*

There's no subtlety, no casting of doubt. No tricks of the serpent. His wife sinned and he readily joined in immediately. Of his own free will.

Many such cases. Misery loves company and the sin of those around us, like the little leaven that leavens the whole lump, it spreads.

*And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons*.

So, having sinned and felt the conviction in their hearts, they knew they were naked before God, and ashamed. Having the knowledge of good and evil, just as the serpent said, using that seed of truth to say it would make them like God.

This is another favorite deception of the devil, to make us covetous of God, and the false promises that we can become God and usurp His station and take His power for ourselves.

And the first instinct Adam and Eve had, when faced with this feeling of shame, was to attempt to cover it up with their own works. In aprons they made. And like our own works, the fig leaves were insufficient to make them righteous. And seeing that the LORD God was in the garden, they hid from Him, showing that they knew in their hearts their work wasn't enough.

God calls to them, and calls them out for their transgression of the law, (*for sin is the transgression of the law*), and questions them, if they ate of that tree He forbid.

And Adam, like many of us when caught up in sin, blames another, and in fact, blames God.

*The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.*

It's her fault. And you gave me her, so it's really your fault, God!

How often do we rationalize our sins this way? How laughable it is when Adam does it. It's cringe, embarrassing, to see him, who given everything and free will, still has the audacity to blame the God who created him for his own choices.

"Oh if I had this advantage" and "If things were different and I didn't have this pressure on me..." "If this person didn't give me the opportunity, the temptation, oh Lord! The person you brought in to my life, I might add!"

And Eve answers no better; *The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.* Her own covetousness playing no part in her excuse.

How many times in our lives have we, like Adam, blamed the cruel fates and fallen nature of others, and the God who made us for our willful and intentional sin? Or blame the devil for tricking us into doubting God's word, beguiled.

It's as pathetic and stupid as when Adam and Eve do it here.

And how many of us seeking our own righteousness, poorly sow together fig leaves of our own works, seeking to erase the transgressions ourselves. Hiding from God?

So having sinned and fallen, God the Father who loves man, offers the first promise of Christ, while laying out the consequences of bringing sin into the world.

To the devil, that old serpent, *Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.*

I plan on expounding on the seed of the woman/seed of the devil, Revelation 12 and how this promise is fulfilled in Jesus in another post.  But note that the seed who bruises Satan's head, and whom Satan bruises the heel, is Christ.

To Eve, *I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.*

Women know pain and complications of childbirth in ways few creatures in creation can. And their season of fertility, more frequent, and their conceptions, multiplied. And by their nature, they shall desire their husbands will.

This last part deserves its own post as well. Both the meaning and implications of this desire, and how man's failure subverts and damages relationships, twisting this God given inclination in woman. (I would also note modern Bible versions change this verse to have opposite meaning, and how that undermines everything).

And to man, through Adam, we are punished;

*Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life; Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field; In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.*

The consequences of sin is death. We return to the ground whereof we were made, after a lifetime of labor to feed ourselves and survive. With the very things of nature we had dominion over, turned against us. Struggle. Death. The wages of sin.

But here, in **Genesis 3**, at the very beginning of mankind as a fallen creature, loved by God, He covers our sins.

 *Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them.*

Shedding of blood for the remission of sin. Covered by the righteousness of the lamb, slain before the foundation of the world. God gives them this gift, freely. Of His own handiwork, not ours.

And so we are now, still naked. Still in sin. Our nature, made manifest in Adam, to choose struggle and death over obedience. Unable to cover our shame by our own works, and needing instead the gift of God, the blood of Christ, covered in the spotless coat of the lamb, slain without blemish. Given the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ as a gift from a loving and merciful God.

This is the Gospel. This is the same faith, as received by Adam, and passed on to his descendents, who call upon the name of the Lord to be saved, and becoming sons of God.

 *But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name.*

Amen

It should not have to be said that the perverted and disgusting false doctrine that Eve had relations with the serpent is from the pitts of Hell and those damned reprobates who promote it are to be rejected, utterly.

Yes, there are children of the devil. They are those who are reprobate, given up and given over by God. They are of their father, the devil. Sons of Belial. That synagogue of Satan. It isn't a physical seed, but a spiritual one, and they don't reproduce, the recruit though guile, trauma, abuse, and appeals to the flesh. And they seek to do his will, and are at enmity with God and with humanity. Murderers from the first.

**John 8:44**
*Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.*

What Jesus says here about Satan is literally true. This is not hyperbole and railing, but Christ putting Satan, and his seed, in perspective referencing **Genesis 3**.

The seed of the serpent, a spiritual seed made up of reprobates throughout scripture, doing the lusts of their father. At enmity with mankind. Hating Jesus.

Satan was a murderer from the beginning. His first act we witness is his tempting Eve to sin, knowing her spiritual and physical death the wage for her and Adam's sin. He murdered them. Being the father of lies, telling the first lie as the means of murder.

*And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel....And Adam called his wife's name Eve; because she was the mother of all living.*

**Psalm 2**

*Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine a vain thing? The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the Lord, and against his anointed, saying, Let us break their bands asunder, and cast away their cords from us.*

*He that sitteth in the heavens shall laugh: the* Lord *shall have them in derision.Then shall he speak unto them in his wrath, and vex them in his sore displeasure.*

*Yet have I set my king upon my holy hill of Zion. I will declare the decree: the* Lord *hath said unto me, Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee.*

*Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel.*

*Be wise now therefore, O ye kings: be instructed, ye judges of the earth.Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice with trembling.*

*Kiss the Son, lest he be angry, and ye perish from the way, when his wrath is kindled but a little. Blessed are all they that put their trust in him.*

**Revelation 12**

*And there appeared a great wonder in heaven; a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and upon her head a crown of twelve stars:*

*2 And she being with child cried, travailing in birth, and pained to be delivered.*

*3 And there appeared another wonder in heaven; and behold a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns upon his heads.*

*4 And his tail drew the third part of the stars of heaven, and did cast them to the earth: and the dragon stood before the woman which was ready to be delivered, for to devour her child as soon as it was born.*

All of Genesis, as important as the stories of Adam, Cain, Noah, the flood and Babel are, was prologue to this. The story of Abram and Sarai. Abraham and Sarah.

Up to this point, mankind who called upon the name of the Lord had the promise of His blessing and protection, of God being their savior, but not the specific promise of the man Christ Jesus. Born of man. Seed of Abraham. Here we see that the LORD appears unto Abram and makes him promises.

- I will make of thee a great nation
 - I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing
- I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee:
- and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.

These are direct blessings and promises to Abram, himself. Many try to take the personal promise to Abraham, to bless those that bless him and curse those that curse him, and claim it's an eternal promise to the modern Jew and the apostate state calling itself Israel. This is found no where in Scripture. This is God's promise to protect him and his wife, as God has called Abraham to go to a different land, to Canaan, and there He would establish his legacy.

*And Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother's son, and all their substance that they had gathered, and the souls that they had gotten in Haran; and they went forth to go into the land of Canaan.*

There, God appeared again to him, and gave this more specific promise; *Unto thy seed will I give this land: and there builded he an altar unto the Lord, who appeared unto him.* *And Abram called upon the name of the Lord.*

He was saved by faith through grace. Note the timing of when that was. It comes up later in scripture.

This promise was made to a 75yr old, childless Abram in a place where *the Canaanite was then in the land.* His altar built between the Mediterranean and Jordan, between Galelee and Jerusalem.

The LORD appearing to Abraham is considered by many to be an Old Testament appearance of Jesus. A theophany. As the Bible says at no time has man seen the Father, many consider the appearance of God unto man in the OT a representation of Christ, who was from the beginning with God and is God.

Next we are given a familiar story of a famine in the land, of going to Egypt to sojourn. Of Pharoah and plagues. This theme of finding refuge and sojourning in Egypt is a picture of young Jesus being taken there by Joseph, just as Jesus' stepfather's namesake will.

There in Egypt, worried that Sarai, his 65yo wife, who was still apparently very fair to look upon, would be taken from him, and that he would be killed, Abram tells her to lie and say they are siblings.

This seems to be a lack of faith by Abram, and causes enmity with Pharoah, who indeed was going to seek to betroth Sarai, but now, subject to plagues by the LORD, angrily asks them to leave the shelter of his kingdom.

God cursed those who would curse Abram, despite his lapse of faith. God made that promise to him, and if he trusted God, he wouldn't fear for his life. As it stood, God came through anyway, but Abram and all his household were sent away back to Canaan and the famine.

God makes promises to us who believe; to be blessed, to be heirs, to be a blessing to others, to be protected by Him in faith and saved from death, in the imputed righteousness of Jesus. By His grace and mercy.

Unfortunately, like Abram, a man of great faith, many of us have doubts. We try to arrange matters and control circumstances out of fear. Sometimes even with convenient lies.

We see with Abram, who by faith moved his entire house to a strange land at the behest of God, was never told to go to Egypt in the first place. Let alone to lie to save his own skin.

We should not fear famines or tribulations or even persecution of unregenerate man. We should be faithful unto death, convinced of the hope that we shall be delivered.

But even Abram, the father of the seed that contained Christ incarnate, doubted and was weak. But we will see, his faith grew stronger the more he walked with God.

Bookends of faith, a covenant fufifiled.

Now, as the Bible in **Galatians 4** says, regarding the story of Sarah and Isaac, that these things be an allegory, the children of the promise in Sarah, the children after the bondage of the law, in Hagar. That the true seed of Abraham isn't after the flesh, as Ishmael was by the bondwoman Hagar, but by the miracle of God, Issac, conceived in faith through Sarah.

The life story of Sarah represents Old Testament Israel, faithful believing Israel, who were saved through faith in the promise made to Abraham. An allegory, as the Bible says.

When we first meet Sarah, as a young wife to Abraham, we are told she was barren. Without hope of conception. She journeys to Canaan, the promised land.

Later, due to famine, she sojourns into Egypt, is captured by Pharaoh, and God for Sarah's sake visits plagues upon the Pharoah's house until he relents and sends Sarah, Abraham, Lot and their cattle and belongings out from Egypt. Just as the Israelites spoiled Egypt, and went out with them, a mixed multitude.

Sarah, despite her faith and love of God lapses in faith, and brings adultery to the bed of Abraham, with Hagar. Sarah's impatience with God's promise has her seek to find an heir after the flesh. Just as the Israelites lapsed in faith and brought the adultery of strange gods at times, and eventually sought an earthly king to rule them, frustrated at the timing of God.

And like Israel, which would at times repent and turn back to God, admitting their error, Sarah says to Abraham; *My wrong be upon thee: I have given my maid into thy bosom; and when she saw that she had conceived, I was despised in her eyes: the Lord judge between me and thee.*

And Hagar, having fled from Sarah with Ishmael the heir after the law, representing Israel after the flesh, not of faith, was given another chance by God, so too were the Jews of Jesus earthly ministry, to receive the adoption by faith that they though was theirs by law. And Sarah, believing Israel, gave them a home until the coming of Isaac.

We are told of another captivity, Sarah taken by a king, and freed not by plagues but by the fear of the Lord upon Abimelech, convicted of his error, just as Babylonian captivity was.

And when Isaac was born, Ishmael mocked the heir of the promise, and Sarah cast out the bondwoman and her son, though it grieved Abraham, the father. But God agrees with Sarah that son after the flesh, the heir according to the law be cast out, so that the son of faith may come in to his inheritance in full. Just as the non-believing Jews were cut off.

(God, in His mercy offers salvation to Hagar if she just believe. And a well of water giving her salvation, just as any seed of Abraham after the flesh can still repent towards Christ today)

Finally, Sarah having seen her son born of a miracle and come to be offered as a sacrifice, (I believe at 33 upon a hill in Jerusalem, spared by God, a picture of Jesus) she passes away a year later, at 127 years old and is honored, being given a place with the patriarchs, our being told of her end, chronicled by scripture. And in her faith, she was saved, and through her, all nations and kindreds were blessed.

And so with this better understanding of the allegory, of recognizing that the entire Old Testament is about Christ Jesus and salvation by faith alone in him, to redeem us, offered by God the father in love and grace, we can understand the righteous anger of Paul writing unto the Galatians.

The Church of the Galatians being swayed by judaizers into accepting another gospel, one of bondage to the law. Whereby they were being told that they must circumcise, keep the days and the months and the dietary laws in the carnal ordinances to be saved. Being dragged back to Hagar, the Bond woman and rejecting Sarah and the son of the promise. Of faith.

And Paul writes, "*O foolish Galatians! who hath bewitched you, that ye should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you?"* The Apostle is angry, he says he fears them. He says that he doubts their salvation, which he had labored with them and questions if it was in vain. Paul saying that only an unsaved person who didn't believe the gospel of Faith he presented them would be susceptible to the judaizers dragging them back under the law and away from the liberty of Christ.

*My little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you,I desire to be present with you now, and to change my voice; for I stand in doubt of you.*

 *Tell me, ye that desire to be under the law, do ye not hear the law?*

*For it is written, that Abraham had two sons, the one by a bondmaid, the other by a freewoman.*

*But he who was of the bondwoman was born after the flesh; but he of the freewoman was by promise.*
*Which things are an allegory: for these are the two covenants.*

He says that he's willing to go through this again with them that they may come to Jesus. That they seeking to be brought back under the law, he says don't you even hear the law? And this is what prompts his use of Sarah and Hagar as an allegory. As a teaching moment taken from scripture that they may understand the difference between salvation by faith alone and the bondage of the law.

This is the same message we can give to those claiming Christ who have added works of the law to the salvation given in the simple Gospel of reconciliation and faith.

These judaizers and those bewitched by them will claim that, "Yes it's by faith alone but you have to do the works of the law to be saved. You have to adhere to our vain traditions. To our carnal ordinances. To our dietary restrictions. You don't expect to just be handed salvation? Do you?"

And so they bring people to be the seed after Hagar, not Sarah. And like Ishmael, they do not receive the inheritance which is given by faith in God's promise, not by heirs according to the law.

Just as Sarah was barren from birth, and brought to old age, it took a miracle of God, visited upon her, to bring her the promise. Not by anything she did, for she was not capable, but in God all things are possible.

This is the lesson. *Do you not hear the law?*

If you're trusting in your own works, if you're sewing your own fig leaves, if you're offering the fruit of your garden, instead of the firstling of the flock, if you're committing adultery with Hagar to produce your salvation, repent. Hear the law.

Salvation is given us by God, in His grace, through His Son, Jesus Christ, killed for our sins, a burnt offering, raised from the dead, that we may be redeemed in faith and sealed by the Holy Spirit unto the day of redemption. A free gift that once accepted cannot be lost. Eternal life. Heir to the Kingdom. Sons of God.

Issac, at 60 years old, finally becomes a father. In an echo of his own birth, Rebekah is as barren as Sarah was. Yet God intervenes, and the couple conceive twin boys.

As God says to Rebekah, there are two nations striving within her. One shall be strong, and the elder will serve the younger.

Esau, the first born, hair red as the pottage he'd sell his birthright for. Red is the meaning of Edom. Jacob, second born, holding on to Esau's foot, as they are taken from their mother.

*And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents.*
*And Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison: but Rebekah loved Jacob.*

God wastes no time on irrelevant details. Isaac's life story is briefly skimmed over. Only the details of the inheritance and blessing matter to the story God is telling. Of the elder serving the younger. Of the law and of faith.

And so, we come to adult Esau and Jacob, men established as a hunter, and a man of the field, while the younger tends flocks, living in tents. No great hero and hunter, proficient with weapons like his elder brother, but a plain man.

Jacob makes a red pottage, a lentil soup. Esau, hungry and tired, saying "*Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage; for I am faint*."

Most interpret this to just mean normal hunger. Not truly fainting or starving in a serious sense. Just ravenous from being out in the field hunting, and wanting to please his flesh by eating the pottage.

Jacob says he will feed his brother in exchange for his birthright. And despising his birthright, that is not caring about it, willing to trade it for a momentary satisfaction of the flesh, Esau agrees.

Paul uses this illustration in **Hebrews 12** regarding fornicators among the believers, who have the inheritance but lose the blessings that come with the birthright we share in Christ Jesus for the same momentary satisfaction of the flesh. That later, though he repented of giving away his inheritance by law to his younger brother, having a change of heart too late, and losing the eventual blessings meant for him.

Christians who live carnally, after the flesh, despising their birthright received through Christ, losing blessings of God for their own morsel of meat, a simple bowl of pottage, are like Esau. And while we still retain sonship, and gain a share in the kingdom, the blessings we lose here in this life and in the time to come are lost or diminished, regardless of how tearfully we may regret it when our flesh dies. It's a grave warning.

We know, having hindsight what a fool Esau, now Edom was. Yet how many times do we do the same, for much less than even a bowl of lentils?

Now, the Bible says that God hated Esau, and Jacob He loved. This is referring to the nations that come from each, Jacob giving birth to the 12 patriarchs of Israel, Esau the nations of Edomites. Much is made of this distinction, but the fate of Edom is not necessarily reflected in the life of its patriarch, Esau. In the next chapter we will look more closely at that.

For now, the parallels to Cain and Abel, Sarah and Hagar, Isaac and Ismael, Jews and Gentiles, even Jesus and Barabbas, the free will choices given to show that God favors faith over the law, spirit over the flesh, blesses them that trust His promises and do His will, giving them the inheritance for their faith, and the casting out of those who are after the flesh, even if by law they have a birthright claim.

The entire Old Testament serves as a pattern for the salvation to come offered in Christ. Both the choice to believe, placing faith above flesh, explaining the theology of the New Testament with examples from the Old. And continually we see the eldest by law passed over, to serve the younger, who by faith receives both the birthright and blessing.

When applied to the Jews and Gentiles, this is called "replacement theology," which is a misnomer. Like Esau, Jews sought an earthly kingdom from an earthly messiah, to satisfy their fleshly desires. They sold their birthright, despising their inheritance, by choosing to kill Christ. By rejecting the blessing that had carried them from Canaan to Egypt, back to the promised land. Through wars, invasions and captivity, they lost everything, for the younger, the Gentiles, to gain.

It's not replacement, it's rejection. Spiritual Edom. And like Edom after the flesh, they were made desolate by the Lord.

Moses was writing this to the Israelites who were to come into the promised land, and a warning and application of not being diluted as a people by intermarriage with the heathen was necessary. Unequal yoke marriage is still relevant today. And the spoiling of a daughter should still provoke wrath in men, rather than quiet acceptance of fornication.

Jacob tells them that their actions have endangered them all in the land they'd not yet been given. That they shared with other people.

I really appreciate how God doesn't just show us perfect people, cardboard villains and heroes. These are real people with complex character and who do wicked things out of the abundance of their hearts, and yet find grace in God and His blessings when they turn to him.

Joseph testing and messing with his brothers at first, only to relent as he sees Benjamin and wanting to see his father, still alive. Through all of it Joseph's faith in God carried him. Amen.

This type of epic historical narrative puts to shame the sinful Hollywood fiction they feed us.

And so, the penultimate chapter of Genesis. Israel lay dying, and he brings his 12 sons together for his last words, and prophetic blessing, *that which shall befall* them *in the last days*.

To his first born of Leah, Reuben he begins by complimenting his eldest son, but quickly turns to his indecisive nature and the grave sin he committed in **Genesis 35:22**;

*And it came to pass, when Israel dwelt in that land, that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father's concubine: and Israel heard it.*

The worst of this was Israel dwelt in that land, at that time, for his beloved wife Rachel's funeral. Reuben there for the occasion took and knew his father's concubine and mother of his brothers. Israel says of his son "thou shall not excel." He does not receive the double portion or blessing allotted the first born and his people have nothing special about their future.

Simeon and Levi, instruments of cruelty Israel calls them for their slaughter of the Hivites in **Genesis 34** as retribution for when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took Dinah, and lay with her, and defiled her, taking their sister's honor. Even after seeking restitution as God commands, to marry her and pay dowry. Treacherous murder in their anger, and this denies them the double portion and the blessing as well. Israel prophesies that they will be divided and scattered.

The tribe of Simeon, according to the book of Judges[,](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book_of_Judges) locates its territory in the promised land inside the boundaries of the Tribe of Judah. It is usually counted as one of the "ten lost tribes," gradually being assimilated into Judah over time.

The tribe of Levi was destined to be made the priests of Israel, owning no land, scattered throughout the remaining tribes.

Judah, the 4th son by Leah, receives a single portion of the inheritance but gains the blessing, the promise of Christ in his lineage. The lion of Judah is another name of Jesus.
